statement: hibernation_available() is a four-way conjunction: hibernation not disabled on the command line, lockdown not covering LOCKDOWN_HIBERNATION, no live secretmem, no active CXL memory.
hibernate(), the resume initcall and the /sys/power/disk and /sys/power/resume stores all check hibernation_available().
nohibernate sets both noresume and nohibernate: it disables hibernation and resume.
hibernate= tests its value by prefix in the order noresume, nocompress, no, protect_image: hibernate=nocompress only stops compression; any other value starting no disables hibernation and resume.
quote: if (!strncmp(str, "noresume", 8)) { noresume = 1; } else if (!strncmp(str, "nocompress", 10)) { nocompress = 1; } else if (!strncmp(str, "no", 2))

statement: noresume sets only noresume: hibernation stays available but the resume initcall bails out, so the last image is not read at boot.
quote: If the user said "noresume".. bail out early.

statement: LOCKDOWN_HIBERNATION precedes LOCKDOWN_INTEGRITY_MAX, integrity is level LOCKDOWN_INTEGRITY_MAX, and a reason is refused when kernel_locked_down >= what: integrity lockdown already blocks hibernation.
quote: Lockdown reasons that protect kernel integrity (ie, the ability for userland to modify kernel code) are placed before LOCKDOWN_INTEGRITY_MAX.

statement: This host's kernel lockdown level is none.
secretmem and CXL blockers are not in the gate's facts; /sys/power/disk prints [disabled] whenever hibernation_available() is false at read time.

statement: lockdown= takes integrity or confidentiality; the effective level is the bracketed word of /sys/kernel/security/lockdown.
quote: Enable the kernel lockdown feature. If set to integrity, kernel features that allow userland to modify the running kernel are disabled.
